messages:
maria: Heads-up — I captured an nsys + perfetto run for the KV-cache regression on g4-8 last night. Trace is ~1.2GB (nsys.qdstrm). Where should I put it and what do we need to scrub?

kevin: put it in the internal traces bucket: s3://redwood-internal-traces/eng-runtime/. But please follow naming + redact rules.

samir: quick note on the trace itself — kernel timeline shows a lot of small cublasLt GEMM launches around the cache-miss spikes. Might be kernel selection thrash.

maria: thanks. I want to upload the raw bundle but need to remove customer dataset paths and S3 ARNs first. Any existing script?

jen: use the trace-redact helper. It strips absolute paths, S3 ARNs, and AWS account ids. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal-tools/tree/main/trace-redact (run locally before uploading).

perf-bot: recommended upload path and naming pattern: 
`s3://redwood-internal-traces/eng-runtime/{year}/{month}/{day}/{root_ts}-{uploader}-{short-desc}-{trace-type}.qdstrm`
Example: `.../2026/03/17/1815000000-maria-kvcache-nsys.qdstrm`
Please include a one-line summary in the object metadata: kernel-hotspot=cublasLt_gemm, kvcache-miss=true, batch-config=auto-32

kevin: question: nvprof vs nsys vs perfetto — which artifact do we prefer for handoff? I have both nvprof CSVs and the nsys.qdstrm.

samir: prefer nsys + perfetto timeline. nsys has the kernel metrics we need (latency, occupancy, L2 usage) and perfetto gives the UI for the KV cache timeline overlay. Keep nvprof CSVs if you want low-level counters, but nsys is primary.

maria: here's the capture command I used (for reference):
```bash
# record CUDA kernels + unified perf, include API
nsys profile -o /tmp/1815000000-maria -t cuda,osrt,nvtx,cuda_memcpy --sample=none --trace=cpu,cuda --stop-after true -- ./run_inference_workload.sh
# convert to qdstrm bundle for upload
nsys export --output /tmp/1815000000-maria.qdstrm /tmp/1815000000-maria.nsys-rep
```

jen: scrub steps I run: 1) run trace-redact on qdstrm 2) gzip 3) create a small README.txt with probed command and a 1-line summary 4) upload to the path perf-bot suggested 5) paste the s3 link in this thread and ping @eng-runtime.

maria: doing that now. One more: any rules about including full command line with AWS creds? I definitely need to strip env vars.

perf-bot: absolutely strip envs and credential files. The redact tool removes known env var patterns and common credential file names (.aws/credentials). If you used KMS keys, list the KMS key id only (no key material).

maria: uploaded scrubbed bundle: s3://redwood-internal-traces/eng-runtime/2026/03/17/1815000000-maria-kvcache-nsys.qdstrm.gz and added README with: "short: kvcache-regression, kernel-hotspot=cublasLt_gemm, note=kv-flush-misalignment"

ops-bot: Upload detected for object s3://redwood-internal-traces/eng-runtime/2026/03/17/1815000000-maria-kvcache-nsys.qdstrm.gz (size: 350MB after gzip). Tagged: eng-runtime-trace, scrubbed=true.

kevin: awesome — can someone annotate the perfetto timeline with KV cache events (kv-get, kv-put, flush) so we can align with kernel launches?

samir: I can add annotations. If you include an events.csv with timestamped KV events (columns: us_ts, event, key-shard) we can import into perfetto as a custom track. Prefer microsecond timestamps aligned to system clock used when trace captured.

maria: will add events.csv to the bundle. One last thing: naming for short-desc should be human readable no spaces, use hyphens.

jen: yes: use hyphens, lowercase, and the root_ts prefix like perf-bot suggested. That's what our triage scripts expect.

samir: after I annotate I'll run a quick kernel selection audit: dump the kernel selectors used during the run and see if there's repeated fallback selections. If we see selector churn at sequence lengths X,Y we should add a pinned-kernel entry for that profile.

maria: thanks all — I'll post the perfetto URL once annotated. If anyone wants the raw nvprof CSVs, DM me. :thumbsup:
